subject: Re: SLA credits and uptime target - NovaCloud procurement
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@novacloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novacloud.com
Date: 2026-04-12T09:14:00Z
Subject: SLA - uptime target & credit calc

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team here is excited about the latency profile you showed. Procurement asked me to open a short thread to confirm a few SLA items before we move to signature:

1) Uptime: Our security team is asking for a 99.99% monthly uptime commitment for the hosted API (pinned model). Your standard template lists 99.95% — can you share options to get to 99.99% (or what exceptions would apply)?

2) Measurement window & exclusions: We need clarity on scheduled maintenance windows and whether multi-tenant capacity degradation is included in downtime calculations.

3) Credits: Procurement expects a straightforward monthly credit table (e.g., % of monthly fee per 30-minute block below SLA). Your template looks different from what our legal expects. Can you propose concrete % credits for each tier?

We can be flexible on price if we get stronger availability guarantees, but we need the calc to be predictable. Attaching our procurement checklist as a reference (not attached here).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if easier.

—Ethan
Director, Cloud Ops
NovaCloud Solutions
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@novacloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-12T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA - uptime target & credit calc

Ethan — thanks for laying this out. Short answers up front: we can discuss a narrower exception to the 99.95% baseline for dedicated/reserved capacity customers; 99.99% is achievable but usually requires reserved capacity + small price adjustment and an agreed maintenance window/notification process.

I'm looping legal (Laura) and our infra lead (Marcus) to draft a concrete proposal for the credit table and exclusions. Please see below for a couple of clarifying Qs that will affect the credit tiers:

- Do you expect the SLA to apply to all API endpoints or only the model-serving endpoints for the pinned model?
- Is NovaCloud planning to use Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) or Hosted API? Dedicated makes 99.99% much easier to commit to.

If you prefer, we can propose two options: Hosted 99.95% (standard credits), Dedicated 99.99% (reduced credits + commit). Laura — could you draft the redline language and a credit table? Marcus — any engineering caveats we should call out (maintenance windows, force majeure)?

I'll compile and send a proposed redline by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@novacloud.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-13T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA - uptime target & credit calc

Ethan / team — sending a first-pass redline and suggested credit schedule (attached). Highlights:

- Baseline: Hosted API (multi-tenant) — 99.95% monthly uptime; Credits: 10% monthly service fee for <99.95-99.80, 25% for <99.80-99.00, 50% below 99.00.
- Dedicated/reserved pool: we can offer 99.99% for customers committing to a 6- or 12-month reserved agreement. Proposed credits: 5% for 99.99-99.975, 15% for 99.975-99.90, 40% below 99.90.
- Scheduled maintenance: we propose a 4-hour monthly scheduled maintenance exclusion for dedicated customers with 72-hour notice; for Hosted customers, 6 hours with 48-hour notice.
- Measurement: downtime is measured at the platform ingress for the affected region; partial degradation (increased p95 latency under agreed thresholds) will be treated as a separate latency SLA (see clause 4).
- Latency commitments: we are willing to provide p95 latency commitments for dedicated customers (example: p95 < 250ms for typical text-gen workloads at up to N QPS — subject to model and sequence length).

Attachment: SLA_Redline_NovaCloud_v2.docx (redline with wording and the credit table). I also attached a simple calculator (SLA-credit-calculator.xlsx) showing how monthly credits would be applied pro rata against the committed monthly invoice.

Ethan — can you confirm which deployment model NovaCloud expects? That will determine which option we should mark up.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@novacloud.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novacloud.com
Date: 2026-04-14T15:35:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA - uptime target & credit calc

Laura / Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear table. A few points from procurement:

- NovaCloud will request Dedicated (reserved) for the production tenant. We can commit to a 12-month term if we get the 99.99% language and a clear credit table.
- Concern: the proposed 4-hour monthly maintenance exclusion is acceptable, but we need the right to a pro-rated credit if maintenance extends beyond notice windows or if multiple maintenances stack.

Also, legal wants a clear measurement cadence and transparency: we need the monthly availability report (CSV) and an API or portal access to the uptime metrics (ideally an S3 export). Is that something you can commit to?

If you can accept the 12-month reserved + 99.99% with the credit table you proposed (with an added clause for stacked maintenance), I can push this to signature next week.

—Ethan
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@novacloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-15T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA - uptime target & credit calc

Ethan — this is great, thanks. Quick internal summary and proposed commitments we can sign up to: 

1) Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved 12-month commit) — we will commit to 99.99% monthly uptime for the dedicated tenant.

2) Credits: use the Dedicated credit table Laura proposed, with one edit: add a clause that if scheduled maintenance windows exceed the notice/length thresholds or two maintenances overlap and cause cumulative downtime beyond the exclusion, credits will apply pro rata for the incremental downtime.

3) Measurement & transparency: we will provide a monthly availability CSV export and a read-only dashboard link. We can provide an S3 export workflow during onboarding (security/vpc-appropriate mechanism).

4) Latency: we will include a p95 latency clause for the agreed model/sequence envelope in the SOW; this will be operationalized in the runbook and observed during the onboarding phase.

Attached are the redline doc and the credit calc. If that looks good I can send a final redline for signature and loop in finance for the reserved capacity invoice. Happy to take a 20-minute call tomorrow to finalize any last items.

Attachments: SLA_Redline_NovaCloud_v2.docx; SLA-credit-calculator.xlsx

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0122
